model: Distressed going concern scenario model: insolvency creditor waterfall bear, risked owner FCF recovery base and bull (engine route)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report cash flow statement share-based payment add-back (A$3.3m); no equity-award withholding taxes disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0 across the history)
inputs.share_count_basis: Ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026: 2,867.7m opening + 3,750.0m issued 26 Nov 2025 on conversion of the Bally's / Investment Holdings notes = 6,617.7m. No dilutive performance rights at balance date (FY2026 AR EPS note). NOT the 5,097.7m weighted average in the Metrics CSV, which understates the count by 23%. Held flat in the recovery scenarios; the PIK liability of A$11.4m that is to be settled in shares (subject to AGM approval, October 2026) is carried as debt instead of as shares.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T05:19:53Z regular ASX close (last bar; volume normal, not a frozen quote)
inputs.wacc_rationale: 10.0% in AUD for all three scenarios: AU 10-year government bond ~4.4% + 6% ERP x ~1.2 unlevered-to-target casino beta gives a cost of equity near 11.5%, blended with normal (not current) secured debt cost at a 25% target weight. Distress risk is charged ONCE, in the scenario weights (35% to an equity-nil insolvency) and in an explicit bridge deduction for the 14% coupon, not in the discount rate. No per-scenario WACC differences.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities of A$15.3m are inside total_debt and no lease principal is deducted from the flows. Immaterial either way.
inputs.net_debt_composition: Debt at face: USD 390m term facility = A$565.2m at the 30 June 2026 spot of 0.69 (carrying value A$544.9m is net of A$23.0m unamortised borrowing costs) + A$11.4m PIK/subordinated balance + A$15.3m leases = A$591.9m. Cash: A$267.1m cash and equivalents + A$100.5m restricted deposits (interest reserve account and guarantee backing) = A$367.6m. Restricted deposits are included because they pre-fund interest that an unlevered DCF does not otherwise charge. Cash had fallen to A$192.4m by 31 July 2026 after the NSW duty payment; that outflow is captured through the regulatory-provision deduction in the bridge, not by restating cash.
inputs.base_revenue_basis: Normalised net revenue A$1,101.0m (excludes A$205.2m of DBC contracted cost recoveries that are passed through at cost with no margin). Statutory continuing revenue is A$1,306.2m; margins in the driver paths are on the normalised base, on which FY2026 EBITDA before significant items was -A$16.1m (-1.5%).
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. The routing table offers two rows and SGR straddles them. It is not in receivership, not suspended from quotation and both casinos are open and trading, so the pure 'asset or creditor waterfall' row would ignore a live operating business that new controlling holders (Bally's 37.8%, Investment Holdings/Mathieson) recapitalised with A$300m in 2025. But the FY2026 accounts carry a material-uncertainty going-concern paragraph, net current liabilities of A$222.3m, an undecided AUSTRAC penalty (A$100m argued by Star vs A$400m by AUSTRAC), both casino licences suspended under a Manager / Special Manager, and a 14% secured USD facility with EBITDA and asset-coverage covenants first tested Dec 2026 - Mar 2027. A three-growth-scenario owner-FCF DCF would treat insolvency as a slow-growth case. So the parts are combined: the BEAR is the distressed-row outcome (creditor waterfall, equity nil) and BASE and BULL are owner-FCF recoveries run through the component engine, with regulatory provisions, the above-market coupon and non-operating assets handled in the equity bridge. The bear's driver path is CALIBRATED, not forecast: it describes the enterprise as it would run under lender or new-owner control (EBITDA margin plateauing at 13% on a lower revenue base), which is worth about A$460m against roughly A$437m of net claims ranking ahead of ordinary shares, so creditors recover about par and existing equity gets nil (A$0.00 per share). A literal cash-burn path makes the engine print a negative share value (-A$0.10), which limited liability rules out and which would drag the weighted value below what a shareholder can actually lose. A finding that follows: bear and base operating paths differ by only about one point of mature margin and some revenue, because the equity is a thin residual over the claims. SBC is tiny (A$3.3m, 0.3% of revenue); the EBITDA margin paths are stated after it and the explicit SBC row is 0%, so house and street values coincide and band_position is null (the band collapsed). Buybacks of A$1.7m are treasury-share purchases for employee plans, not a repurchase programme. Tax: A$248.9m of tax-effected losses are unrecognised; cash tax is held at zero for five years in base and ramped to 30%, shorter than the losses would allow because the 2025 change of control puts the continuity-of-ownership test in doubt. POST-BALANCE-DATE EVENTS NOT VERIFIED: no Analysis JSON existed and web search returned nothing, so the outcome of the AUSTRAC judgment, the 30 September 2026 licence / Manager decisions, the transactional banking extension and any Q1 FY2027 trading update are unknown to this model. Any of them can move the weights materially.

equity_bridge.item: Regulatory and legal provisions and other creditors (AUSTRAC provision, NSW underpaid duty, NICC fines)
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 AR note B6 closing balance. Debt-like: cash claims not in the forward flows. Split not disclosed; actual AUSTRAC penalty may differ materially.

equity_bridge.item: Above-market coupon on USD term facility to May 2029
equity_bridge.note: Term SOFR + 10% (~14%) on A$565m vs ~8% normal secured cost: ~A$34m/yr excess for 2.9 years, discounted. Unlevered flows at a 10% WACC do not otherwise charge it; no tax shield while loss-making.

equity_bridge.item: Investments in associates and joint ventures at book (mainly Destination Gold Coast Consortium)
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 balance sheet. Equity-accounted, so its results are outside EBITDA.

equity_bridge.item: Assets held for sale net of liabilities (Stage 2 JVP assets: Treasury Brisbane hotel and car parks)
equity_bridge.note: 83.1 less 5.3. Stage 2 completion expected by 31 March 2027, subject to conditions precedent.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: scenario judgment; no historical CAGR is usable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-36% to -40%) diverges from revenue CAGR (-3% to -11%) by far more than 30%: book value was destroyed by ~A$3.9bn of impairments and penalties, not by revenue decline. EPS and owner FCF are negative at both ends of every window, so their CAGRs are undefined. Historical growth is not an input to this valuation.
historical_growth.notes: Statutory revenue FY2021 1,545.4, FY2023 1,867.5, FY2026 1,306.2 (continuing, includes pass-through cost recoveries). Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC): FY2023 -94.1, FY2024 -31.9, FY2025 -214.5, FY2026 -80.6. Reported FCF is levered (after interest paid).

base.narrative: Survives; licences reinstated; margins recover to roughly half the pre-crisis level.
base.sbc_note: SBC row held at 0%: the EBITDA margin path is stated AFTER share-based payments (A$3.3m, 0.3% of revenue in FY2026), so the cost is charged once, inside the margin. House and street values therefore coincide.

bull.narrative: Full turnaround under Bally's: Sydney regains share and margins return to FY2023 domestic levels.
bull.sbc_note: SBC row held at 0%: the EBITDA margin path is stated AFTER share-based payments (A$3.3m, 0.3% of revenue in FY2026), so the cost is charged once, inside the margin. House and street values therefore coincide.

bear.narrative: Insolvency or wipe-out recapitalisation: the enterprise continues under creditor control and is worth about the claims ahead of equity; existing shares get nil. Path calibrated to that waterfall.
bear.sbc_note: SBC row held at 0%: the EBITDA margin path is stated AFTER share-based payments (A$3.3m, 0.3% of revenue in FY2026), so the cost is charged once, inside the margin. House and street values therefore coincide.

scenario_narratives.base: Star survives without a further wipe-out raise. The AUSTRAC penalty lands near the provision and is payable over time; the Sydney and Gold Coast licences are reinstated as the remediation plan completes; covenants are met or waived. FY2027 revenue slips 2% as the Brisbane operator fee steps down from A$59.7m to a fixed A$18m plus incentive, offset by the slots growth and corporate cost-out seen in 2H FY2026. EBITDA margin climbs from -1% to 14% by year 7: Sydney back to low-teens property margins under mandatory carded play and A$1,000 cash limits, Gold Coast mid-teens as the precinct towers open. That is roughly A$200m of EBITDA in year 10 against A$520m in FY2019, because the VIP/junket business is gone for good, NSW duty is higher and clubs and pubs keep uncarded machines. Capex returns to 5% of revenue from the starved 3% of FY2026. No cash tax for five years on unrecognised losses.
scenario_narratives.bull: Bally's operating control delivers a full domestic turnaround. The penalty is at the low end with a long payment schedule, licences are reinstated in 2027, the 14% facility is refinanced early at a normal cost, and carded-play rules are extended to clubs and pubs so the playing field levels. Sydney regains table and slot share, Gold Coast benefits from full ownership of the DGCC precinct after Stage 2, and the Brisbane incentive fee starts to pay. EBITDA margin reaches 19% by year 7, about A$300m by year 10, comparable to the FY2023 domestic run-rate of the same properties before cash limits.
scenario_narratives.bear: The AUSTRAC judgment is at or near A$400m and payable on a schedule Star cannot fund (it told the Court more than A$100m within 12 months would be challenging); or EBITDA stays near zero through FY2027 and the minimum-EBITDA covenant (from 31 March 2027) or the 1.40x asset-coverage test (31 December 2026) is breached; or a regulator declines reinstatement; or transactional banking is withdrawn. Any one of these puts the first-ranking USD lender in control. The casinos do not close: they are run on by the lender or a new owner after an enforcement, a debt-for-equity swap or a rescue raise priced at cents. The driver path is that enterprise: revenue falls 5% and 2% before stabilising, EBITDA margin recovers only to 13%, and the business is worth about A$460m. Claims ranking ahead of ordinary shares are about A$437m before any penalty above the provision (A$592m debt less A$368m cash, A$375m regulatory creditors, A$85m excess coupon, less A$248m of non-operating assets), so creditors recover roughly par and existing equity recovers nothing. The per-share value is nil; the path is calibrated to that waterfall and is not an operating forecast.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 35%, well above the 15% default: the auditor has flagged material going-concern uncertainty, the directors' own solvency opinion is conditional on four separate things going right (penalty quantum and timing, a return to profitability sufficient for covenants, licence reinstatement, banking continuity), and the company is burning cash on a 14% facility. Base 45%: the 2025-26 recapitalisation, the DBC exit and guarantee release, and the improvement in EBITDA from -A$76m to -A$16m show the survival path is real and has committed sponsors. Bull 20%, below the 35% default, because it needs several independent outcomes at once: a low penalty, early refinancing, regulatory change affecting competitors and a share recovery in Sydney.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Star is valued as a distressed going concern, not as a normal operating company and not as a dead shell. The equity is an option on survival: if the business fails the shares are worth nothing, and if it survives the value is whatever a structurally smaller, more heavily regulated two-casino operator earns after regulatory creditors, a 14% secured loan and the 3.75bn shares issued in the rescue. The bear scenario is therefore a creditor waterfall with equity at nil; base and bull are owner-FCF recoveries on the house engine with distress handled in the weights and the equity bridge instead of the discount rate. The model's conclusion is that the market capitalisation of about A$1.1bn (6.6bn shares) already pays for more than the bull case; the low per-share price is an artefact of an eightfold increase in the share count since FY2016, not evidence of cheapness.
valuation_philosophy.model_choice_reasoning: Considered and rejected: (1) standard three-scenario owner-FCF DCF - treats insolvency as slow growth and lets a negative-FCF bear either run away or sit on a floor without saying equity is wiped; (2) pure asset/creditor waterfall - book equity of A$377.5m (A$0.057 per share) is a residual of heavily impaired, licence-dependent property whose realisable value in enforcement is unknown, and it ignores a recapitalised operating business; (3) raising WACC to 15-20% - charges distress in the rate and again in the scenarios. Chosen: scenario model straddling the 'distressed' and 'operating company, non-US' rows of the routing table.
key_risks_to_valuation: AUSTRAC penalty quantum and payment timing: the single largest swing factor; A$400m against a provision whose AUSTRAC component is undisclosed would likely force a rescue raise or enforcement
Covenants on the USD term facility: 1.40x asset coverage tested 31 December 2026, minimum EBITDA from 31 March 2027, minimum liquidity stepping from A$50m to A$100m
Licence reinstatement in NSW and Queensland; Manager and Special Manager terms ran to 30 September 2026 and the outcome is not known to this model

Further dilution: any equity raise at or below the A$0.08 conversion price used in 2025 would cut per-share value even in a survival scenario; the flat share count is the most optimistic assumption in base and bull

Upside not modelled: Pyrmont and Gold Coast real estate and development rights may be worth more than impaired book value; a control bid by Bally's; the low free float can hold the price above fundamental value for long periods
AUD/USD: the debt is in USD and unhedged in this model; each 1c fall in AUD adds about A$8m to debt
Post-balance-date events (AUSTRAC judgment, licence decisions, Q1 FY2027 trading) could not be verified at the valuation date

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 0.083-0.195
data_sources.financials: SGR.AX_Metrics.csv and the FY2026 Annual Report (balance sheet, notes A2, A7, B6, B7, C2, F6, going-concern note), Q3 FY2026 quarterly update
data_sources.qualitative: FY2026 Annual Report directors' report and going-concern note; no Analysis JSON was available; web search for post-balance-date events returned nothing
